title: MapReduce, Shuffle & Distributed Aggregation
interviewAnswer: MapReduce partitions map work, groups intermediate keys through a shuffle, then reduces grouped values. Modern engines generalize this DAG model, but shuffle remains a major network/disk cost.
keyPoints: Map is embarrassingly parallel; shuffle is expensive.
why: MapReduce, Shuffle & Distributed Aggregation appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.

deepDive: MapReduce partitions map work, groups intermediate keys through a shuffle, then reduces grouped values. Modern engines generalize this DAG model, but shuffle remains a major network/disk cost. Partitioning and skew dominate performance. Combiners/pre-aggregation can reduce traffic. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Compute counts by key across terabytes: local maps emit counts, shuffle groups keys, reducers sum them.
